pt.title: [Logística 101 #2] A Escassez de Leite de Aveia Que Ninguém Pediu: Gestão da Cadeia de Suprimentos, Explicado

segments.src: > A supply chain is every company it takes to turn dirt into a product on your shelf — and the reason a small blip in demand can turn into a factory-sized panic.
segments.tr: > Uma cadeia de suprimentos é toda empresa necessária para transformar matéria-prima em um produto na sua prateleira — e a razão pela qual um pequeno desvio na demanda pode se transformar em um pânico do tamanho de uma fábrica.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Conceito do Dia

segments.src: Most people picture a supply chain as a truck.
segments.tr: A maioria das pessoas imagina uma cadeia de suprimentos como um caminhão.

segments.src: It's actually a **network of companies** — farms, factories, warehouses, carriers, retailers — passing goods, money, and information to each other until something lands in your hands.
segments.tr: Na verdade, é uma **rede de empresas** — fazendas, fábricas, armazéns, transportadoras, varejistas — passando bens, dinheiro e informações uns para os outros até que algo chegue às suas mãos.

segments.src: **The players.** A typical chain has five roles:
segments.tr: **Os atores.** Uma cadeia típica tem cinco papéis:

segments.src: - **Suppliers** — raw materials and components. The company that sells directly to the manufacturer is a *tier-1 supplier*; the company that supplies *them* is tier-2, and so on down.
segments.tr: - **Fornecedores** — matérias-primas e componentes. A empresa que vende diretamente ao fabricante é um *fornecedor de nível 1*; a empresa que os fornece é nível 2, e assim por diante.

segments.src: - **Manufacturer** — turns inputs into finished goods.
segments.tr: - **Fabricante** — transforma insumos em produtos acabados.

segments.src: - **Distributor / wholesaler** — buys in bulk, breaks it into store-sized quantities, holds inventory.
segments.tr: - **Distribuidor / atacadista** — compra em grande quantidade, divide em quantidades de tamanho de loja, mantém inventário.

segments.src: - **Retailer** — sells to you. Amazon, Kroger, the corner bodega.
segments.tr: - **Varejista** — vende para você. Amazon, Kroger, a pequena loja da esquina.

segments.src: - **Customer** — you. The only person in the chain who actually *creates* demand. Everyone upstream is guessing at what you'll do.
segments.tr: - **Cliente** — você. A única pessoa na cadeia que realmente *cria* demanda. Todos a montante estão adivinhando o que você fará.

segments.src: Alongside all of them sit **3PLs** (third-party logistics providers) — UPS, XPO, C.H.
segments.tr: Ao lado de todos eles estão os **3PLs** (provedores de logística de terceiros) — UPS, XPO, C.H.

segments.src: Robinson — companies that don't own the product but move and store it.
segments.tr: Robinson — empresas que não são donas do produto, mas o movem e armazenam.

segments.src: **Value chain vs.
segments.tr: **Cadeia de valor vs.

segments.src: supply chain.** Easy to confuse.
segments.tr: cadeia de suprimentos.** Fácil de confundir.

segments.src: The *supply chain* is who does what, physically.
segments.tr: A *cadeia de suprimentos* é quem faz o quê, fisicamente.

segments.src: The **value chain** (Michael Porter's 1985 framing) asks a different question: at each step, how much value gets added versus how much it costs?
segments.tr: A **cadeia de valor** (estrutura de Michael Porter de 1985) faz uma pergunta diferente: em cada etapa, quanto valor é agregado versus quanto custa?

segments.src: A $5 bag of coffee beans might carry 40 cents of farming and $1.80 of roasting, packaging, and brand.
segments.tr: Um saco de $5 de grãos de café pode ter 40 centavos de cultivo e $1.80 de torrefação, embalagem e marca.

segments.src: Supply chain thinking asks "how do we move it?"
segments.tr: O pensamento da cadeia de suprimentos pergunta "como movemos isso?"

segments.src: Value chain thinking asks "where are we actually making money?"
segments.tr: O pensamento da cadeia de valor pergunta "onde realmente estamos ganhando dinheiro?"

segments.src: **Three flows, not one.** Product flows downstream toward the customer.
segments.tr: **Três fluxos, não um.** O produto flui para jusante em direção ao cliente.

segments.src: Money flows upstream.
segments.tr: O dinheiro flui para montante.

segments.src: **Information flows both ways** — and that third flow is where supply chains break.
segments.tr: **As informações fluem nos dois sentidos** — e esse terceiro fluxo é onde as cadeias de suprimentos quebram.

segments.src: **The bullwhip effect.** Here's the central idea of this lesson.
segments.tr: **O efeito chicote.** Aqui está a ideia central desta lição.

segments.src: When information gets distorted as it travels up the chain, order swings get *amplified* at every hop.
segments.tr: Quando as informações se distorcem ao viajar pela cadeia, as oscilações de pedidos são *amplificadas* em cada salto.

segments.src: A small wiggle at the retail end becomes a violent crack at the factory end — like snapping a whip.
segments.tr: Uma pequena oscilação no final do varejo se torna um crack violento no final da fábrica — como estalar um chicote.

segments.src: The pattern was first modeled by MIT's Jay Forrester in the early 1960s.
segments.tr: O padrão foi modelado pela primeira vez por Jay Forrester do MIT no início dos anos 1960.

segments.src: The name stuck after Procter & Gamble noticed that Pampers sales at stores were steady while orders hitting their plants swung wildly.
segments.tr: O nome pegou depois que Procter & Gamble notou que as vendas de Pampers nas lojas eram estáveis enquanto os pedidos chegando em suas plantas oscilavam descontroladamente.

segments.src: In 1997, Hau Lee and colleagues at Stanford named four causes:
segments.tr: Em 1997, Hau Lee e colegas em Stanford nomearam quatro causas:

segments.src: 1. **Demand forecast updating** — every tier forecasts off the orders it receives, not off real customer demand. You're forecasting a forecast.
segments.tr: 1. **Atualização de previsão de demanda** — cada nível faz previsões baseadas nos pedidos que recebe, não na demanda real do cliente. Você está prevendo uma previsão.

segments.src: 2. **Order batching** — nobody orders 3 units; they wait and order a full truckload once a month. Smooth demand goes out as lumpy orders.
segments.tr: 2. **Lote de pedidos** — ninguém pede 3 unidades; eles esperam e pedem um carregamento completo uma vez por mês. A demanda suave sai como pedidos desiguais.

segments.src: 3. **Price fluctuation** — promotions and discounts cause "forward buying." Retailers stock up cheap, then order nothing for six weeks.
segments.tr: 3. **Flutuação de preço** — promoções e descontos causam "compra antecipada." Os varejistas fazem estoque barato, depois não pedem nada por seis semanas.

segments.src: 4. **Shortage gaming** — when supply is tight and gets rationed proportionally, buyers inflate orders to claim a bigger slice, then cancel.
segments.tr: 4. **Jogo de escassez** — quando o suprimento é limitado e é racionado proporcionalmente, os compradores inflam os pedidos para reivindicar uma fatia maior, depois cancelam.

segments.src: A rough way to measure it:
segments.tr: Uma forma aproximada de medir:

segments.src: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE
segments.tr: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE

segments.src: Above 1.0 means you're amplifying.
segments.tr: Acima de 1.0 significa que você está amplificando.

segments.src: Every tier above 1.0 multiplies onto the next.
segments.tr: Cada nível acima de 1.0 se multiplica para o próximo.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## No Dia a Dia

segments.src: A café in Denver sells about **100 cartons of oat milk a week**, steady, for a year.
segments.tr: Um café em Denver vende cerca de **100 caixas de leite de aveia por semana**, de forma constante, por um ano.

segments.src: Then a cold snap hits and a latte-heavy week pushes sales to **120** — a 20% bump.
segments.tr: Então uma onda de frio chega e uma semana pesada de latte impulsiona as vendas para **120** — um aumento de 20%.

segments.src: The owner doesn't want to run out, so she orders **150**: 120 to cover demand, plus 30 to rebuild a safety cushion.
segments.tr: O proprietário não quer ficar sem estoque, então pede **150**: 120 para cobrir a demanda, mais 30 para reconstruir um amortecedor de segurança.

segments.src: That's a 50% jump in orders.
segments.tr: Esse é um salto de 50% nos pedidos.

segments.src: Her distributor serves 40 cafés doing roughly the same thing.
segments.tr: Seu distribuidor atende 40 cafés fazendo aproximadamente a mesma coisa.

segments.src: Incoming orders leap 50%.
segments.tr: Os pedidos recebidos saltam 50%.

segments.src: The distributor's warehouse is now thin, and lead time from the plant is three weeks — so they order 50% more *plus* three weeks of extra buffer.
segments.tr: O armazém do distribuidor agora está enxuto, e o tempo de entrega da fábrica é de três semanas — então eles pedem 50% mais *mais* três semanas de amortecedor extra.

segments.src: Their order to the plant goes up **90%**.
segments.tr: Seu pedido à fábrica sobe **90%**.

segments.src: The plant in Ohio sees a 90% spike, assumes oat milk is having a moment, books overtime, and orders oat groats and packaging at **double** the normal rate — some of it airfreighted at a premium.
segments.tr: A fábrica em Ohio vê um pico de 90%, assume que o leite de aveia está tendo seu momento, agenda horas extras e pede aveia em grão e embalagem em **dobro** da taxa normal — um pouco sendo transportado por via aérea com prêmio.

segments.src: Meanwhile the weather turns.
segments.tr: Enquanto isso, o tempo muda.

segments.src: Denver goes back to 100 cartons a week.
segments.tr: Denver volta para 100 caixas por semana.

segments.src: The café is sitting on 50 extra cartons with a shelf-life clock running, so it orders **nothing** next week.
segments.tr: O café está sentado em 50 caixas extras com um relógio de vida de prateleira funcionando, então não pede **nada** na próxima semana.

segments.src: The distributor sees zero.
segments.tr: O distribuidor vê zero.

segments.src: The plant sees zero, cancels the overtime, and eats the raw material it just paid a premium for.
segments.tr: A fábrica vê zero, cancela o turno extra e absorve a matéria-prima que acabou de pagar um prêmio.

segments.src: Real customer demand moved **20%, once**.
segments.tr: A demanda real do cliente se moveu **20%, uma vez**.

segments.src: Factory-level demand swung from **+100% to -100%** and back.
segments.tr: A demanda no nível da fábrica oscilou de **+100% a -100%** e voltou.

segments.src: Nobody behaved irrationally.
segments.tr: Ninguém se comportou irracionalmente.

segments.src: Every single person made a locally sensible decision with the information they had.
segments.tr: Cada pessoa tomou uma decisão localmente sensata com as informações que tinha.

segments.src: That's the bullwhip.
segments.tr: Esse é o chicote.

segments.src: And it's why Walmart shares point-of-sale data directly with suppliers, why vendor-managed inventory exists, and why "everyday low pricing" is a supply chain strategy, not just a marketing slogan — it kills cause #3.
segments.tr: E é por isso que o Walmart compartilha dados de ponto de venda diretamente com fornecedores, por que o inventário gerenciado por fornecedor existe, e por que "preço baixo diário" é uma estratégia de cadeia de suprimentos, não apenas um slogan de marketing — mata a causa nº 3.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## Resumo em 3 Linhas

segments.src: 1. A supply chain is a network of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and 3PLs moving three things: product downstream, money upstream, and information both ways.
segments.tr: 1. Uma cadeia de suprimentos é uma rede de fornecedores, fabricantes, distribuidores, varejistas e 3PLs movendo três coisas: produto para jusante, dinheiro para montante e informações nos dois sentidos.

segments.src: 2. The value chain is a different lens on the same steps — it asks where cost is incurred and where value is actually added.
segments.tr: 2. A cadeia de valor é uma lente diferente sobre os mesmos passos — pergunta onde o custo é incorrido e onde o valor é realmente adicionado.

segments.src: 3. The bullwhip effect is demand distortion amplifying upstream; its cure is better shared information, smaller/more frequent orders, stable pricing, and allocation rules that don't reward inflated orders.
segments.tr: 3. O efeito chicote é a distorção da demanda amplificando para montante; sua cura é informações compartilhadas melhores, pedidos menores/mais frequentes, preços estáveis e regras de alocação que não recompensam pedidos inflacionados.

segments.src: **Three flows, not one.** Product flows downstream toward the customer.
segments.tr: **Tiga aliran, bukan satu.** Produk mengalir ke hilir menuju pelanggan.

segments.src: Money flows upstream.
segments.tr: Uang mengalir ke hulu.

segments.src: **Information flows both ways** — and that third flow is where supply chains break.
segments.tr: **Informasi mengalir dua arah** — dan aliran ketiga itulah di mana rantai pasokan rusak.

segments.src: **The bullwhip effect.** Here's the central idea of this lesson.
segments.tr: **Efek bullwhip.** Berikut adalah ide sentral dari pelajaran ini.

segments.src: When information gets distorted as it travels up the chain, order swings get *amplified* at every hop.
segments.tr: Ketika informasi menjadi terdistorsi saat perjalanan naik rantai, ayunan pesanan menjadi *diperkuat* di setiap lompatan.

segments.src: A small wiggle at the retail end becomes a violent crack at the factory end — like snapping a whip.
segments.tr: Sedikit gerakan di ujung ritel menjadi retak kekerasan di ujung pabrik — seperti memukul cambuk.

segments.src: The pattern was first modeled by MIT's Jay Forrester in the early 1960s.
segments.tr: Pola ini pertama kali dimodelkan oleh Jay Forrester dari MIT pada awal 1960-an.

segments.src: The name stuck after Procter & Gamble noticed that Pampers sales at stores were steady while orders hitting their plants swung wildly.
segments.tr: Nama itu melekat setelah Procter & Gamble memperhatikan bahwa penjualan Pampers di toko stabil sementara pesanan yang mengenai pabrik mereka berfluktuasi liar.

segments.src: In 1997, Hau Lee and colleagues at Stanford named four causes:
segments.tr: Pada tahun 1997, Hau Lee dan rekan-rekan di Stanford menyebutkan empat penyebab:

segments.src: 1. **Demand forecast updating** — every tier forecasts off the orders it receives, not off real customer demand. You're forecasting a forecast.
segments.tr: 1. **Pembaruan prakiraan permintaan** — setiap tingkat meramalkan dari pesanan yang diterima, bukan dari permintaan pelanggan nyata. Anda meramalkan prakiraan.

segments.src: 2. **Order batching** — nobody orders 3 units; they wait and order a full truckload once a month. Smooth demand goes out as lumpy orders.
segments.tr: 2. **Pengelompokan pesanan** — tidak ada yang memesan 3 unit; mereka menunggu dan memesan truk penuh sekali sebulan. Permintaan halus keluar sebagai pesanan yang tidak rata.

segments.src: 3. **Price fluctuation** — promotions and discounts cause "forward buying." Retailers stock up cheap, then order nothing for six weeks.
segments.tr: 3. **Fluktuasi harga** — promosi dan diskon menyebabkan "pembelian maju." Pengecer menyimpan murah, kemudian tidak memesan selama enam minggu.

segments.src: 4. **Shortage gaming** — when supply is tight and gets rationed proportionally, buyers inflate orders to claim a bigger slice, then cancel.
segments.tr: 4. **Permainan kekurangan** — ketika pasokan ketat dan dibatasi secara proporsional, pembeli menaikkan pesanan untuk mengklaim irisan yang lebih besar, kemudian membatalkan.

segments.src: A rough way to measure it:
segments.tr: Cara kasar untuk mengukurnya:

segments.src: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE
segments.tr: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE

segments.src: Above 1.0 means you're amplifying.
segments.tr: Di atas 1,0 berarti Anda memperkuat.

segments.src: Every tier above 1.0 multiplies onto the next.
segments.tr: Setiap tingkat di atas 1,0 mengalikan ke tingkat berikutnya.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: A café in Denver sells about **100 cartons of oat milk a week**, steady, for a year.
segments.tr: Sebuah kafe di Denver menjual sekitar **100 karton susu oat seminggu**, stabil, selama satu tahun.

segments.src: Then a cold snap hits and a latte-heavy week pushes sales to **120** — a 20% bump.
segments.tr: Kemudian gelombang dingin menimpa dan minggu yang berat latte mendorong penjualan menjadi **120** — kenaikan 20%.

segments.src: The owner doesn't want to run out, so she orders **150**: 120 to cover demand, plus 30 to rebuild a safety cushion.
segments.tr: Pemilik tidak ingin kehabisan, jadi dia memesan **150**: 120 untuk menutupi permintaan, plus 30 untuk membangun kembali bantal keselamatan.

segments.src: That's a 50% jump in orders.
segments.tr: Itu adalah lompatan 50% dalam pesanan.

segments.src: Her distributor serves 40 cafés doing roughly the same thing.
segments.tr: Distributor di melayani 40 kafe melakukan hal yang kurang lebih sama.

segments.src: Incoming orders leap 50%.
segments.tr: Pesanan masuk melompat 50%.

segments.src: The distributor's warehouse is now thin, and lead time from the plant is three weeks — so they order 50% more *plus* three weeks of extra buffer.
segments.tr: Gudang distributor sekarang tipis, dan waktu tunggu dari pabrik adalah tiga minggu — jadi mereka memesan 50% lebih banyak *plus* tiga minggu penyangga tambahan.

segments.src: Their order to the plant goes up **90%**.
segments.tr: Pesanan mereka ke pabrik naik **90%**.

segments.src: The plant in Ohio sees a 90% spike, assumes oat milk is having a moment, books overtime, and orders oat groats and packaging at **double** the normal rate — some of it airfreighted at a premium.
segments.tr: Pabrik di Ohio melihat lonjakan 90%, menganggap susu oat sedang memiliki momen, memesan lembur, dan memesan oat groats dan kemasan dengan tarif **dua kali lipat** — beberapa di antaranya airfreighted dengan harga premium.

segments.src: Meanwhile the weather turns.
segments.tr: Sementara itu cuaca berubah.

segments.src: Denver goes back to 100 cartons a week.
segments.tr: Denver kembali ke 100 karton per minggu.

segments.src: The café is sitting on 50 extra cartons with a shelf-life clock running, so it orders **nothing** next week.
segments.tr: Kafe duduk di atas 50 karton ekstra dengan jam daya tahan rak berjalan, jadi dia tidak memesan apa pun minggu depan.

segments.src: The distributor sees zero.
segments.tr: Distributor melihat nol.

segments.src: The plant sees zero, cancels the overtime, and eats the raw material it just paid a premium for.
segments.tr: Pabrik melihat nol, membatalkan lembur, dan mengonsumsi bahan baku yang baru saja dibayar premium.

segments.src: Real customer demand moved **20%, once**.
segments.tr: Permintaan pelanggan nyata bergerak **20%, sekali**.

segments.src: Factory-level demand swung from **+100% to -100%** and back.
segments.tr: Permintaan tingkat pabrik berfluktuasi dari **+100% hingga -100%** dan kembali.

segments.src: Nobody behaved irrationally.
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang berperilaku irasional.

segments.src: Every single person made a locally sensible decision with the information they had.
segments.tr: Setiap orang membuat keputusan yang masuk akal secara lokal dengan informasi yang mereka miliki.

segments.src: That's the bullwhip.
segments.tr: Itulah bullwhip.

segments.src: And it's why Walmart shares point-of-sale data directly with suppliers, why vendor-managed inventory exists, and why "everyday low pricing" is a supply chain strategy, not just a marketing slogan — it kills cause #3.
segments.tr: Dan itulah mengapa Walmart berbagi data poin penjualan langsung dengan pemasok, mengapa inventori yang dikelola vendor ada, dan mengapa "penetapan harga rendah sehari-hari" adalah strategi rantai pasokan, bukan hanya slogan pemasaran — itu membunuh penyebab #3.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan 3 Baris

segments.src: 1. A supply chain is a network of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and 3PLs moving three things: product downstream, money upstream, and information both ways.
segments.tr: 1. Rantai pasokan adalah jaringan pemasok, produsen, distributor, pengecer, dan 3PL yang memindahkan tiga hal: produk ke hilir, uang ke hulu, dan informasi dua arah.

segments.src: 2. The value chain is a different lens on the same steps — it asks where cost is incurred and where value is actually added.
segments.tr: 2. Value chain adalah lensa yang berbeda pada langkah-langkah yang sama — ia menanyakan di mana biaya dikeluarkan dan di mana nilai benar-benar ditambahkan.

segments.src: 3. The bullwhip effect is demand distortion amplifying upstream; its cure is better shared information, smaller/more frequent orders, stable pricing, and allocation rules that don't reward inflated orders.
segments.tr: 3. Efek bullwhip adalah distorsi permintaan yang memperkuat ke hulu; obatnya adalah informasi bersama yang lebih baik, pesanan yang lebih kecil/lebih sering, penetapan harga yang stabil, dan aturan alokasi yang tidak memberi imbalan pada pesanan yang meningkat.

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **1.** A company that sells components directly to a manufacturer is called a:
segments.tr: **1.** Perusahaan yang menjual komponen langsung ke produsen disebut:

segments.src: - (A) Tier-2 supplier
segments.tr: - (A) Pemasok tingkat-2

segments.src: - (B) Tier-1 supplier
segments.tr: - (B) Pemasok tingkat-1

segments.src: - (C) 3PL
segments.tr: - (C) 3PL

segments.src: - (D) Distributor
segments.tr: - (D) Distributor

segments.src: **2.** O/X — The bullwhip effect happens because someone in the chain is behaving irrationally or incompetently.
segments.tr: **2.** O/X — Efek bullwhip terjadi karena seseorang dalam rantai berperilaku irasional atau tidak kompeten.

segments.src: **3.** Which of the following would most likely *reduce* the bullwhip effect?
segments.tr: **3.** Mana dari berikut yang paling mungkin *mengurangi* efek bullwhip?

segments.src: - (A) Running a deep 30%-off promotion every quarter
segments.tr: - (A) Menjalankan promosi diskon 30% yang dalam setiap kuartal

segments.src: - (B) Switching from weekly orders to one large monthly truckload
segments.tr: - (B) Beralih dari pesanan mingguan ke satu pengiriman truk bulanan besar

segments.src: - (C) Sharing real point-of-sale data with upstream suppliers
segments.tr: - (C) Berbagi data poin penjualan nyata dengan pemasok ke hulu

segments.src: - (D) Allocating scarce supply in proportion to order size
segments.tr: - (D) Mengalokasikan pasokan langka sebanding dengan ukuran pesanan

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Supply chain** — The network of organizations that moves a product from raw material to end customer.
segments.tr: - **Rantai pasokan** — Jaringan organisasi yang memindahkan produk dari bahan baku ke pelanggan akhir.

segments.src: - **Value chain** — A framework for analyzing where cost is added and where value is created across a firm's activities.
segments.tr: - **Value chain** — Kerangka kerja untuk menganalisis di mana biaya ditambahkan dan di mana nilai diciptakan di seluruh kegiatan perusahaan.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — The upstream amplification of demand variability caused by distorted information.
segments.tr: - **Efek bullwhip** — Amplifikasi ke hulu dari variabilitas permintaan yang disebabkan oleh informasi yang terdistorsi.

segments.src: - **Lead time** — The elapsed time between placing an order and receiving it; longer lead times force bigger buffers and worsen the bullwhip.
segments.tr: - **Waktu tunggu** — Waktu yang telah berlalu antara penempatan pesanan dan penerimaannya; waktu tunggu yang lebih lama memaksa penyangga yang lebih besar dan memperburuk bullwhip.

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics)** — An outside provider that handles transportation, warehousing, or fulfillment on a company's behalf.
segments.tr: - **3PL (logistik pihak ketiga)** — Penyedia luar yang menangani transportasi, pergudangan, atau pemenuhan atas nama perusahaan.

segments.src: *정답: 1) B — tier numbering counts hops away from the manufacturer, so the direct supplier is tier-1.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: 1) B — penomoran tingkat menghitung lompatan jauh dari produsen, jadi pemasok langsung adalah tingkat-1.

segments.src: 2) X — the whole point is that bullwhip emerges from locally rational decisions; each tier optimizes with only the information it can see.
segments.tr: 2) X — semuanya adalah bahwa bullwhip muncul dari keputusan yang rasional secara lokal; setiap tingkat mengoptimalkan hanya dengan informasi yang dapat dilihatnya.

segments.src: 3) C — shared POS data lets upstream partners forecast off real demand instead of off someone else's order.
segments.tr: 3) C — data POS bersama memungkinkan mitra ke hulu meramalkan permintaan nyata alih-alih pesanan orang lain.

segments.src: (A) is price fluctuation, (B) is order batching, and (D) is exactly the rationing rule that triggers shortage gaming — all three are classic bullwhip causes.*
segments.tr: (A) adalah fluktuasi harga, (B) adalah pengelompokan pesanan, dan (D) adalah aturan pembatasan yang memicu permainan kekurangan — ketiga-tiganya adalah penyebab bullwhip klasik.*

ja.title: [ロジスティクス101 #2] 誰も注文していなかったオーツ麦ミルク不足:サプライチェーン管理について解説

segments.src: > A supply chain is every company it takes to turn dirt into a product on your shelf — and the reason a small blip in demand can turn into a factory-sized panic.
segments.tr: > サプライチェーンは、土から棚の商品に変わるまでに関わるすべての企業を指し、需要のわずかな変動が工場規模のパニックに変わる理由でもあります。

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 本日の概念

segments.src: Most people picture a supply chain as a truck.
segments.tr: ほとんどの人はサプライチェーンをトラックだと考えています。

segments.src: It's actually a **network of companies** — farms, factories, warehouses, carriers, retailers — passing goods, money, and information to each other until something lands in your hands.
segments.tr: 実は**企業のネットワーク**です—農場、工場、倉庫、運送業者、小売業者—商品、お金、情報を互いに受け渡し、最終的にあなたの手に届くまで続きます。

segments.src: **The players.** A typical chain has five roles:
segments.tr: **プレイヤー。** 典型的なチェーンには5つのロールがあります:

segments.src: - **Suppliers** — raw materials and components. The company that sells directly to the manufacturer is a *tier-1 supplier*; the company that supplies *them* is tier-2, and so on down.
segments.tr: - **サプライヤー** — 原材料と部品。製造業者に直接販売する企業は*1次サプライヤー*です;その企業に供給する企業は2次サプライヤーで、以下同様です。

segments.src: - **Manufacturer** — turns inputs into finished goods.
segments.tr: - **製造業者** — 投入資源を完成品に変えます。

segments.src: - **Distributor / wholesaler** — buys in bulk, breaks it into store-sized quantities, holds inventory.
segments.tr: - **流通業者/卸売業者** — 大量購入し、店舗用の数量に分割して、在庫を保有します。

segments.src: - **Retailer** — sells to you. Amazon, Kroger, the corner bodega.
segments.tr: - **小売業者** — あなたに販売します。Amazon、Kroger、街角のお店など。

segments.src: - **Customer** — you. The only person in the chain who actually *creates* demand. Everyone upstream is guessing at what you'll do.
segments.tr: - **顧客** — あなたのことです。実際に需要を*生み出す*唯一の人です。上流のすべての人はあなたが何をするかを推測しているだけです。

segments.src: Alongside all of them sit **3PLs** (third-party logistics providers) — UPS, XPO, C.H.
segments.tr: これらすべてと同時に座る**3PL**(第3者物流提供者)—UPS、XPO、C.H.

segments.src: Robinson — companies that don't own the product but move and store it.
segments.tr: Robinson—商品を所有しないが移動・保管する企業です。

segments.src: **Value chain vs.
segments.tr: **バリューチェーン vs.

segments.src: supply chain.** Easy to confuse.
segments.tr: サプライチェーン。** 混同しやすいですね。

segments.src: The *supply chain* is who does what, physically.
segments.tr: *サプライチェーン*は、物理的に誰が何をするかです。

segments.src: The **value chain** (Michael Porter's 1985 framing) asks a different question: at each step, how much value gets added versus how much it costs?
segments.tr: **バリューチェーン**(マイケル・ポーター1985年のフレーミング)は異なる質問をします:各ステップで、コストはいくらでどれだけの価値が追加されるのか?

segments.src: A $5 bag of coffee beans might carry 40 cents of farming and $1.80 of roasting, packaging, and brand.
segments.tr: 5ドルのコーヒー豆の袋は、農業に40セント、焙煎・包装・ブランドに1.80ドルが含まれる可能性があります。

segments.src: Supply chain thinking asks "how do we move it?"
segments.tr: サプライチェーン思考は「どうやって移動させるか?」と聞きます。

segments.src: Value chain thinking asks "where are we actually making money?"
segments.tr: バリューチェーン思考は「実際にどこで利益を作っているのか?」と聞きます。

segments.src: **Three flows, not one.** Product flows downstream toward the customer.
segments.tr: **3つのフロー、1つではありません。** 製品は下流方向に顧客に流れます。

segments.src: Money flows upstream.
segments.tr: お金は上流に流れます。

segments.src: **Information flows both ways** — and that third flow is where supply chains break.
segments.tr: **情報は双方向に流れます** — そしてその3番目のフローがサプライチェーンが壊れる場所です。

segments.src: **The bullwhip effect.** Here's the central idea of this lesson.
segments.tr: **ブルウィップ効果。** これが今回のレッスンの中心的な考えです。

segments.src: When information gets distorted as it travels up the chain, order swings get *amplified* at every hop.
segments.tr: 情報がチェーンに沿って上がるときに歪むと、注文の変動は各ステップで*増幅*されます。

segments.src: A small wiggle at the retail end becomes a violent crack at the factory end — like snapping a whip.
segments.tr: 小売側のわずかな変動は工場側での激しい変動になります—鞭を打つみたいに。

segments.src: The pattern was first modeled by MIT's Jay Forrester in the early 1960s.
segments.tr: このパターンはMITのジェイ・フォレスターが1960年代初期に最初にモデル化しました。

segments.src: The name stuck after Procter & Gamble noticed that Pampers sales at stores were steady while orders hitting their plants swung wildly.
segments.tr: プロクター・ギャンブルがPampers(パンパース)の店舗での売上は安定していたのに、工場に届く注文が大きく変動していることに気づいた後、この名前が定着しました。

segments.src: In 1997, Hau Lee and colleagues at Stanford named four causes:
segments.tr: 1997年、スタンフォード大学のハウ・リーと同僚たちが4つの原因を名付けました:

segments.src: 1. **Demand forecast updating** — every tier forecasts off the orders it receives, not off real customer demand. You're forecasting a forecast.
segments.tr: 1. **需要予測の更新** — すべての階層は実際の顧客需要ではなく、受け取った注文から予測します。予測の予測をしているのです。

segments.src: 2. **Order batching** — nobody orders 3 units; they wait and order a full truckload once a month. Smooth demand goes out as lumpy orders.
segments.tr: 2. **注文のまとめ買い** — 誰も3ユニットを注文しません;月に1回、完全な1トラック分の注文を待ってから注文します。滑らかな需要がぼこぼこした注文として出ていきます。

segments.src: 3. **Price fluctuation** — promotions and discounts cause "forward buying." Retailers stock up cheap, then order nothing for six weeks.
segments.tr: 3. **価格変動** — プロモーションと割引は"先買い"を引き起こします。小売業者は安く在庫を積み上げ、その後6週間何も注文しません。

segments.src: 4. **Shortage gaming** — when supply is tight and gets rationed proportionally, buyers inflate orders to claim a bigger slice, then cancel.
segments.tr: 4. **配分ゲーミング** — 供給が限定的で比例的に配分されるとき、買い手は注文を水増ししてより大きなシェアを得ようとし、その後キャンセルします。

segments.src: A rough way to measure it:
segments.tr: これを測定するおおよその方法:

segments.src: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE
segments.tr: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE

segments.src: Above 1.0 means you're amplifying.
segments.tr: 1.0以上は増幅していることを意味します。

segments.src: Every tier above 1.0 multiplies onto the next.
segments.tr: 1.0以上のすべての階層が次に乗じられます。

segments.src: Nobody behaved irrationally.

segments.src: And it's why Walmart shares point-of-sale data directly with suppliers, why vendor-managed inventory exists, and why "everyday low pricing" is a supply chain strategy, not just a marketing slogan — it kills cause #3.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3行のまとめ

segments.src: 1. A supply chain is a network of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and 3PLs moving three things: product downstream, money upstream, and information both ways.
segments.tr: 1. サプライチェーンはサプライヤー、製造業者、流通業者、小売業者、3PLのネットワークで、3つのもの—製品を下流に、お金を上流に、情報を双方向に—を移動させます。

segments.src: 2. The value chain is a different lens on the same steps — it asks where cost is incurred and where value is actually added.

segments.src: 3. The bullwhip effect is demand distortion amplifying upstream; its cure is better shared information, smaller/more frequent orders, stable pricing, and allocation rules that don't reward inflated orders.
segments.tr: 3. ブルウィップ効果は需要の歪みが上流で増幅されることです;その治療法は、より良い情報共有、より小さい/より頻繁な注文、安定した価格設定、および水増しされた注文に報いない配分ルールです。

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 本日の用語

segments.src: - **Lead time** — The elapsed time between placing an order and receiving it; longer lead times force bigger buffers and worsen the bullwhip.

de.title: [Logistik 101 #2] Der Hafermilchmangel, den niemand bestellt hat: Supply-Chain-Management erklärt

segments.src: > A supply chain is every company it takes to turn dirt into a product on your shelf — and the reason a small blip in demand can turn into a factory-sized panic.
segments.tr: > Eine Lieferkette ist jedes Unternehmen, das benötigt wird, um Erde in ein Produkt in deinem Regal zu verwandeln — und der Grund, warum eine kleine Nachfrageschwankung in fabrikgroße Panik verwandelt werden kann.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Heutiges Konzept

segments.src: Most people picture a supply chain as a truck.
segments.tr: Die meisten Menschen stellen sich eine Lieferkette als einen Lastwagen vor.

segments.src: It's actually a **network of companies** — farms, factories, warehouses, carriers, retailers — passing goods, money, and information to each other until something lands in your hands.
segments.tr: Es ist tatsächlich ein **Netzwerk von Unternehmen** — Farmen, Fabriken, Lagerhäuser, Frachtführer, Einzelhändler — die Waren, Geld und Informationen untereinander weitergeben, bis etwas in deine Hände landet.

segments.src: **The players.** A typical chain has five roles:
segments.tr: **Die Akteure.** Eine typische Kette hat fünf Rollen:

segments.src: - **Suppliers** — raw materials and components. The company that sells directly to the manufacturer is a *tier-1 supplier*; the company that supplies *them* is tier-2, and so on down.
segments.tr: - **Lieferanten** — Rohstoffe und Komponenten. Das Unternehmen, das direkt an den Hersteller verkauft, ist ein *Tier-1-Lieferant*; das Unternehmen, das *sie* beliefert, ist Tier-2 und so weiter.

segments.src: - **Manufacturer** — turns inputs into finished goods.
segments.tr: - **Hersteller** — wandelt Eingaben in fertige Waren um.

segments.src: - **Distributor / wholesaler** — buys in bulk, breaks it into store-sized quantities, holds inventory.
segments.tr: - **Distributor / Großhändler** — kauft in großen Mengen, teilt es in ladengerechte Mengen auf, hält Bestände.

segments.src: - **Retailer** — sells to you. Amazon, Kroger, the corner bodega.
segments.tr: - **Einzelhändler** — verkauft an dich. Amazon, Kroger, die kleine Eckkneipe.

segments.src: - **Customer** — you. The only person in the chain who actually *creates* demand. Everyone upstream is guessing at what you'll do.
segments.tr: - **Kunde** — du. Die einzige Person in der Kette, die tatsächlich *Nachfrage* erzeugt. Jeder weiter oben rät, was du tun wirst.

segments.src: Alongside all of them sit **3PLs** (third-party logistics providers) — UPS, XPO, C.H.
segments.tr: Neben all diesen sitzen **3PLs** (Drittanbieter-Logistikdienstleister) — UPS, XPO, C.H.

segments.src: Robinson — companies that don't own the product but move and store it.
segments.tr: Robinson — Unternehmen, die das Produkt nicht besitzen, aber transportieren und lagern.

segments.src: **Value chain vs.
segments.tr: **Wertschöpfungskette vs.

segments.src: supply chain.** Easy to confuse.
segments.tr: Lieferkette.** Leicht zu verwechseln.

segments.src: The *supply chain* is who does what, physically.
segments.tr: Die *Lieferkette* ist, wer was, physisch, tut.

segments.src: The **value chain** (Michael Porter's 1985 framing) asks a different question: at each step, how much value gets added versus how much it costs?
segments.tr: Die **Wertschöpfungskette** (Michael Porters Rahmen von 1985) stellt eine andere Frage: Bei jedem Schritt, wie viel Wert wird hinzugefügt, gegenüber wie viel kostet es?

segments.src: A $5 bag of coffee beans might carry 40 cents of farming and $1.80 of roasting, packaging, and brand.
segments.tr: Ein 5-Dollar-Beutel Kaffeebohnen könnte 40 Cent für Anbau und 1,80 Dollar für Röstung, Verpackung und Marke tragen.

segments.src: Supply chain thinking asks "how do we move it?"
segments.tr: Supply-Chain-Denken fragt "Wie transportieren wir es?"

segments.src: Value chain thinking asks "where are we actually making money?"
segments.tr: Wertschöpfungs-Denken fragt "Wo verdienen wir tatsächlich Geld?"

segments.src: **Three flows, not one.** Product flows downstream toward the customer.
segments.tr: **Drei Flüsse, nicht einer.** Produkt fließt stromabwärts zum Kunden.

segments.src: Money flows upstream.
segments.tr: Geld fließt stromaufwärts.

segments.src: **Information flows both ways** — and that third flow is where supply chains break.
segments.tr: **Information fließt in beide Richtungen** — und dieser dritte Fluss ist, wo Lieferketten brechen.

segments.src: **The bullwhip effect.** Here's the central idea of this lesson.
segments.tr: **Der Peitscheneffekt.** Hier ist die zentrale Idee dieser Lektion.

segments.src: When information gets distorted as it travels up the chain, order swings get *amplified* at every hop.
segments.tr: Wenn Informationen verzerrt werden, während sie die Kette hochreisen, werden Bestellschwankungen bei jedem Sprung *verstärkt*.

segments.src: A small wiggle at the retail end becomes a violent crack at the factory end — like snapping a whip.
segments.tr: Ein kleines Wackeln am Einzelhandelsende wird zu einem gewalttätigen Riss am Fabrikende — wie das Knallen einer Peitsche.

segments.src: The pattern was first modeled by MIT's Jay Forrester in the early 1960s.
segments.tr: Das Muster wurde zuerst von Jay Forrester vom MIT in den frühen 1960er Jahren modelliert.

segments.src: The name stuck after Procter & Gamble noticed that Pampers sales at stores were steady while orders hitting their plants swung wildly.
segments.tr: Der Name blieb hängen, nachdem Procter & Gamble bemerkte, dass Pampers-Verkäufe in Geschäften stabil waren, während Bestellungen ihre Fabriken wild schwankten.

segments.src: In 1997, Hau Lee and colleagues at Stanford named four causes:
segments.tr: 1997 benannten Hau Lee und Kollegen von Stanford vier Ursachen:

segments.src: 1. **Demand forecast updating** — every tier forecasts off the orders it receives, not off real customer demand. You're forecasting a forecast.
segments.tr: 1. **Nachfrage-Prognose-Aktualisierung** — jede Ebene prognostiziert basierend auf den Bestellungen, die sie erhält, nicht auf echte Kundennachfrage. Du prognostizierst eine Prognose.

segments.src: 2. **Order batching** — nobody orders 3 units; they wait and order a full truckload once a month. Smooth demand goes out as lumpy orders.
segments.tr: 2. **Bestellbündelung** — niemand bestellt 3 Einheiten; sie warten und bestellen eine volle Ladung einmal im Monat. Sanfte Nachfrage geht als klumpige Bestellungen heraus.

segments.src: 3. **Price fluctuation** — promotions and discounts cause "forward buying." Retailers stock up cheap, then order nothing for six weeks.
segments.tr: 3. **Preisschwankungen** — Aktionen und Rabatte verursachen "Vorratskauf." Einzelhändler lagern billig auf, dann bestellen nichts für sechs Wochen.

segments.src: 4. **Shortage gaming** — when supply is tight and gets rationed proportionally, buyers inflate orders to claim a bigger slice, then cancel.
segments.tr: 4. **Mangel-Spiele** — wenn das Angebot knapp ist und proportional rationiert wird, blähen Käufer Bestellungen auf, um einen größeren Anteil zu beanspruchen, dann stornieren.

segments.src: A rough way to measure it:
segments.tr: Eine grobe Art, es zu messen:

segments.src: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE
segments.tr: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE

segments.src: Above 1.0 means you're amplifying.
segments.tr: Über 1,0 bedeutet, dass du verstärkst.

segments.src: Every tier above 1.0 multiplies onto the next.
segments.tr: Jede Ebene über 1,0 multipliziert sich zur nächsten.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## Im alltäglichen Leben

segments.src: A café in Denver sells about **100 cartons of oat milk a week**, steady, for a year.
segments.tr: Ein Café in Denver verkauft etwa **100 Packungen Hafermilch pro Woche**, konstant, für ein Jahr.

segments.src: Then a cold snap hits and a latte-heavy week pushes sales to **120** — a 20% bump.
segments.tr: Dann kommt ein Kälteeinbruch und eine latte-intensive Woche treibt den Verkauf auf **120** — ein Anstieg von 20%.

segments.src: The owner doesn't want to run out, so she orders **150**: 120 to cover demand, plus 30 to rebuild a safety cushion.
segments.tr: Der Eigentümer möchte nicht ausverkauft sein, also bestellt sie **150**: 120 zur Deckung der Nachfrage, plus 30 zum Wiederaufbau eines Sicherheitspuffers.

segments.src: That's a 50% jump in orders.
segments.tr: Das ist ein Sprung von 50% bei Bestellungen.

segments.src: Her distributor serves 40 cafés doing roughly the same thing.
segments.tr: Ihr Distributor bedient 40 Cafés, die ungefähr dasselbe tun.

segments.src: Incoming orders leap 50%.
segments.tr: Eingehende Bestellungen springen 50%.

segments.src: The distributor's warehouse is now thin, and lead time from the plant is three weeks — so they order 50% more *plus* three weeks of extra buffer.
segments.tr: Das Lager des Distributors ist nun dünn besetzt, und die Lieferzeit von der Fabrik beträgt drei Wochen — also bestellen sie 50% mehr *plus* drei Wochen zusätzlichen Puffer.

segments.src: Their order to the plant goes up **90%**.
segments.tr: Ihre Bestellung an die Fabrik steigt um **90%**.

segments.src: The plant in Ohio sees a 90% spike, assumes oat milk is having a moment, books overtime, and orders oat groats and packaging at **double** the normal rate — some of it airfreighted at a premium.
segments.tr: Die Fabrik in Ohio sieht einen Anstieg von 90%, nimmt an, dass Hafermilch gerade im Trend ist, bucht Überstunden und bestellt Hafergrütze und Verpackung zum **doppelten** normalen Satz — einiges davon mit Luftfracht zu einem Premium.

segments.src: Meanwhile the weather turns.
segments.tr: Inzwischen wendet sich das Wetter.

segments.src: Denver goes back to 100 cartons a week.
segments.tr: Denver geht zurück zu 100 Packungen pro Woche.

segments.src: The café is sitting on 50 extra cartons with a shelf-life clock running, so it orders **nothing** next week.
segments.tr: Das Café sitzt auf 50 zusätzlichen Packungen mit einer laufenden Verfallszeituhr, also bestellt es **nichts** nächste Woche.

segments.src: The distributor sees zero.
segments.tr: Der Distributor sieht null.

segments.src: The plant sees zero, cancels the overtime, and eats the raw material it just paid a premium for.
segments.tr: Die Fabrik sieht null, storniert die Überstunden und muss die Rohstoffe aufbrauchen, für die sie gerade einen Aufschlag zahlte.

segments.src: Real customer demand moved **20%, once**.
segments.tr: Echte Kundennachfrage bewegte sich **20%, einmal**.

segments.src: Factory-level demand swung from **+100% to -100%** and back.
segments.tr: Nachfrage auf Fabrikebene schwankte von **+100% bis -100%** und zurück.

segments.src: Nobody behaved irrationally.
segments.tr: Niemand verhielt sich irrational.

segments.src: Every single person made a locally sensible decision with the information they had.
segments.tr: Jede einzelne Person traf eine lokal sinnvolle Entscheidung mit den Informationen, die sie hatte.

segments.src: That's the bullwhip.
segments.tr: Das ist der Peitscheneffekt.

segments.src: And it's why Walmart shares point-of-sale data directly with suppliers, why vendor-managed inventory exists, and why "everyday low pricing" is a supply chain strategy, not just a marketing slogan — it kills cause #3.
segments.tr: Und das ist, warum Walmart Point-of-Sale-Daten direkt mit Lieferanten teilt, warum lieferantenverwalteter Bestand existiert, und warum "Alltags-Tiefpreise" eine Lieferkettenstrategie sind, nicht nur ein Marketing-Slogan — es eliminiert Ursache #3.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3-Zeilen-Zusammenfassung

segments.src: 1. A supply chain is a network of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and 3PLs moving three things: product downstream, money upstream, and information both ways.
segments.tr: 1. Eine Lieferkette ist ein Netzwerk von Lieferanten, Herstellern, Distributoren, Einzelhändlern und 3PLs, die drei Dinge bewegen: Produkt stromabwärts, Geld stromaufwärts und Information in beide Richtungen.

segments.src: 2. The value chain is a different lens on the same steps — it asks where cost is incurred and where value is actually added.
segments.tr: 2. Die Wertschöpfungskette ist eine andere Perspektive auf die gleichen Schritte — sie fragt, wo Kosten entstehen und wo Wert tatsächlich hinzugefügt wird.

segments.src: 3. The bullwhip effect is demand distortion amplifying upstream; its cure is better shared information, smaller/more frequent orders, stable pricing, and allocation rules that don't reward inflated orders.
segments.tr: 3. Der Peitscheneffekt ist Nachfrageverzerrung, die stromaufwärts verstärkt wird; seine Heilung ist bessere gemeinsame Information, kleinere/häufigere Bestellungen, stabile Preisgestaltung und Zuordnungsregeln, die aufgeblasene Bestellungen nicht belohnen.

vi.title: [Logistics 101 #2] Cuộc Khủng Hoảng Sữa Yến Mạch Mà Ai Cũng Không Dự Đoán: Quản Lý Chuỗi Cung Ứng Được Giải Thích

segments.src: > A supply chain is every company it takes to turn dirt into a product on your shelf — and the reason a small blip in demand can turn into a factory-sized panic.
segments.tr: > Chuỗi cung ứng là tất cả các công ty cần thiết để biến đất thành một sản phẩm trên kệ của bạn — và lý do tại sao một sự thay đổi nhỏ trong nhu cầu có thể dẫn đến một cuộc hoảng loạn quy mô nhà máy.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Khái Niệm Hôm Nay

segments.src: Most people picture a supply chain as a truck.
segments.tr: Hầu hết mọi người hình dung chuỗi cung ứng là một chiếc xe tải.

segments.src: It's actually a **network of companies** — farms, factories, warehouses, carriers, retailers — passing goods, money, and information to each other until something lands in your hands.
segments.tr: Thực ra đó là một **mạng lưới các công ty** — các nông trại, nhà máy, kho lưu trữ, các nhà vận chuyển, nhà bán lẻ — chuyển giao hàng hóa, tiền và thông tin cho nhau cho đến khi thứ gì đó chạm tay bạn.

segments.src: **The players.** A typical chain has five roles:
segments.tr: **Những người chơi.** Một chuỗi điển hình có năm vai trò:

segments.src: - **Suppliers** — raw materials and components. The company that sells directly to the manufacturer is a *tier-1 supplier*; the company that supplies *them* is tier-2, and so on down.
segments.tr: - **Nhà cung cấp** — nguyên liệu thô và các thành phần. Công ty bán trực tiếp cho nhà sản xuất là *nhà cung cấp cấp 1*; công ty cung cấp cho *họ* là cấp 2, v.v.

segments.src: - **Manufacturer** — turns inputs into finished goods.
segments.tr: - **Nhà sản xuất** — biến đầu vào thành hàng hóa hoàn thành.

segments.src: - **Distributor / wholesaler** — buys in bulk, breaks it into store-sized quantities, holds inventory.
segments.tr: - **Nhà phân phối / nhà bán sỉ** — mua số lượng lớn, chia nhỏ thành số lượng cửa hàng, giữ hàng tồn kho.

segments.src: - **Retailer** — sells to you. Amazon, Kroger, the corner bodega.
segments.tr: - **Nhà bán lẻ** — bán cho bạn. Amazon, Kroger, tiệm tạp hóa góc phố.

segments.src: - **Customer** — you. The only person in the chain who actually *creates* demand. Everyone upstream is guessing at what you'll do.
segments.tr: - **Khách hàng** — bạn. Người duy nhất trong chuỗi thực sự *tạo* nhu cầu. Mọi người phía trên đều đang đoán những gì bạn sẽ làm.

segments.src: Alongside all of them sit **3PLs** (third-party logistics providers) — UPS, XPO, C.H.
segments.tr: Bên cạnh tất cả họ là các **3PL** (nhà cung cấp logistics bên thứ ba) — UPS, XPO, C.H.

segments.src: Robinson — companies that don't own the product but move and store it.
segments.tr: Robinson — các công ty không sở hữu sản phẩm nhưng vận chuyển và lưu trữ nó.

segments.src: **Value chain vs.
segments.tr: **Chuỗi giá trị so với

segments.src: supply chain.** Easy to confuse.
segments.tr: chuỗi cung ứng.** Dễ nhầm lẫn.

segments.src: The *supply chain* is who does what, physically.
segments.tr: *Chuỗi cung ứng* là ai làm gì, về mặt vật lý.

segments.src: The **value chain** (Michael Porter's 1985 framing) asks a different question: at each step, how much value gets added versus how much it costs?
segments.tr: **Chuỗi giá trị** (khung nhìn năm 1985 của Michael Porter) đặt ra một câu hỏi khác: tại mỗi bước, giá trị được thêm vào bao nhiêu so với chi phí?

segments.src: A $5 bag of coffee beans might carry 40 cents of farming and $1.80 of roasting, packaging, and brand.
segments.tr: Một túi cà phê 5 đô la có thể mang 40 xu canh tác và 1,80 đô la rang, đóng gói và nhãn hiệu.

segments.src: Supply chain thinking asks "how do we move it?"
segments.tr: Tư duy chuỗi cung ứng hỏi "chúng ta vận chuyển nó như thế nào?"

segments.src: Value chain thinking asks "where are we actually making money?"
segments.tr: Tư duy chuỗi giá trị hỏi "chúng ta thực sự kiếm tiền ở đâu?"

segments.src: **Three flows, not one.** Product flows downstream toward the customer.
segments.tr: **Ba dòng chảy, không phải một.** Sản phẩm chảy xuôi về phía khách hàng.

segments.src: Money flows upstream.
segments.tr: Tiền chảy ngược dòng.

segments.src: **Information flows both ways** — and that third flow is where supply chains break.
segments.tr: **Thông tin chảy cả hai chiều** — và dòng thứ ba đó là nơi các chuỗi cung ứng bị gãy.

segments.src: **The bullwhip effect.** Here's the central idea of this lesson.
segments.tr: **Hiệu ứng roi queo.** Đây là ý tưởng trung tâm của bài học này.

segments.src: When information gets distorted as it travels up the chain, order swings get *amplified* at every hop.
segments.tr: Khi thông tin bị biến dạng khi di chuyển lên chuỗi, sự dao động của đơn hàng bị *khuếch đại* tại mỗi bước nhảy.

segments.src: A small wiggle at the retail end becomes a violent crack at the factory end — like snapping a whip.
segments.tr: Một dao động nhỏ ở đầu bán lẻ trở thành một cú tát dữ dội ở đầu nhà máy — giống như quẫy roi.

segments.src: The pattern was first modeled by MIT's Jay Forrester in the early 1960s.
segments.tr: Mô hình này lần đầu tiên được mô phỏng bởi Jay Forrester của MIT vào đầu những năm 1960.

segments.src: The name stuck after Procter & Gamble noticed that Pampers sales at stores were steady while orders hitting their plants swung wildly.
segments.tr: Cái tên dính vào sau khi Procter & Gamble nhận thấy rằng doanh số bán Pampers tại các cửa hàng ổn định trong khi các đơn hàng tới các nhà máy của họ dao động dữ dội.

segments.src: In 1997, Hau Lee and colleagues at Stanford named four causes:
segments.tr: Năm 1997, Hau Lee và các đồng nghiệp tại Stanford đặt tên bốn nguyên nhân:

segments.src: 1. **Demand forecast updating** — every tier forecasts off the orders it receives, not off real customer demand. You're forecasting a forecast.
segments.tr: 1. **Cập nhật dự báo nhu cầu** — mỗi cấp dự báo dựa trên các đơn hàng mà nó nhận được, không phải dựa trên nhu cầu khách hàng thực tế. Bạn đang dự báo một dự báo.

segments.src: 2. **Order batching** — nobody orders 3 units; they wait and order a full truckload once a month. Smooth demand goes out as lumpy orders.
segments.tr: 2. **Đặt hàng theo lô** — không ai đặt 3 đơn vị; họ chờ và đặt một chuyến xe tải đầy đủ mỗi tháng. Nhu cầu mịn chuyển thành các đơn hàng gồ ghề.

segments.src: 3. **Price fluctuation** — promotions and discounts cause "forward buying." Retailers stock up cheap, then order nothing for six weeks.
segments.tr: 3. **Biến động giá** — khuyến mãi và chiết khấu gây ra "mua trước". Nhà bán lẻ tích trữ rẻ, sau đó không đặt hàng trong sáu tuần.

segments.src: 4. **Shortage gaming** — when supply is tight and gets rationed proportionally, buyers inflate orders to claim a bigger slice, then cancel.
segments.tr: 4. **Chơi trò thiếu hụt** — khi cung cấp hạn chế và được định tỷ lệ tương ứng, người mua phóng đại các đơn hàng để yêu cầu một phần lớn hơn, sau đó hủy.

segments.src: A rough way to measure it:
segments.tr: Một cách đơn giản để đo nó:

segments.src: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE
segments.tr: bullwhip ratio = variance of orders you PLACE / variance of orders you RECEIVE

segments.src: Above 1.0 means you're amplifying.
segments.tr: Trên 1,0 có nghĩa là bạn đang khuếch đại.

segments.src: Every tier above 1.0 multiplies onto the next.
segments.tr: Mỗi cấp trên 1,0 nhân lên cấp tiếp theo.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## Trong Cuộc Sống Hàng Ngày

segments.src: A café in Denver sells about **100 cartons of oat milk a week**, steady, for a year.
segments.tr: Một quán cà phê ở Denver bán khoảng **100 hộp sữa yến mạch mỗi tuần**, ổn định, trong một năm.

segments.src: Then a cold snap hits and a latte-heavy week pushes sales to **120** — a 20% bump.
segments.tr: Sau đó, một đợt lạnh ập đến và một tuần nặng về cà phê làm doanh số tăng lên **120** — tăng 20%.

segments.src: The owner doesn't want to run out, so she orders **150**: 120 to cover demand, plus 30 to rebuild a safety cushion.
segments.tr: Chủ quán không muốn hết hàng, nên cô ấy đặt **150**: 120 để đáp ứng nhu cầu, cộng thêm 30 để xây dựng lại một bộ đệm an toàn.

segments.src: That's a 50% jump in orders.
segments.tr: Đó là một bước nhảy 50% trong đơn hàng.

segments.src: Her distributor serves 40 cafés doing roughly the same thing.
segments.tr: Người phân phối của cô phục vụ 40 quán cà phê làm những việc tương tự.

segments.src: Incoming orders leap 50%.
segments.tr: Các đơn hàng đến vọt tăng 50%.

segments.src: The distributor's warehouse is now thin, and lead time from the plant is three weeks — so they order 50% more *plus* three weeks of extra buffer.
segments.tr: Kho lưu trữ của nhà phân phối giờ đây mỏng, và thời gian giao hàng từ nhà máy là ba tuần — vì vậy họ đặt hàng 50% nhiều hơn *cộng với* ba tuần bộ đệm bổ sung.

segments.src: Their order to the plant goes up **90%**.
segments.tr: Đơn hàng của họ tới nhà máy tăng **90%**.

segments.src: The plant in Ohio sees a 90% spike, assumes oat milk is having a moment, books overtime, and orders oat groats and packaging at **double** the normal rate — some of it airfreighted at a premium.
segments.tr: Nhà máy ở Ohio nhìn thấy một bước nhảy 90%, giả sử sữa yến mạch đang có xu hướng, đặt công việc ngoài giờ, và đặt hàng yến mạch và bao bì với **gấp đôi** tốc độ bình thường — một số được vận chuyển bằng máy bay với phí bảo hiểm.

segments.src: Meanwhile the weather turns.
segments.tr: Trong khi đó thời tiết thay đổi.

segments.src: Denver goes back to 100 cartons a week.
segments.tr: Denver trở lại 100 hộp mỗi tuần.

segments.src: The café is sitting on 50 extra cartons with a shelf-life clock running, so it orders **nothing** next week.
segments.tr: Quán cà phê có 50 hộp dư thừa với đồng hồ hạn sử dụng chạy, vì vậy cô ấy đặt **không có** tuần tiếp theo.

segments.src: The distributor sees zero.
segments.tr: Nhà phân phối thấy không có.

segments.src: The plant sees zero, cancels the overtime, and eats the raw material it just paid a premium for.
segments.tr: Nhà máy thấy không có, hủy công việc ngoài giờ, và ăn nguyên liệu thô mà nó vừa trả tiền cao cho.

segments.src: Real customer demand moved **20%, once**.
segments.tr: Nhu cầu khách hàng thực tế di chuyển **20%, một lần**.

segments.src: Factory-level demand swung from **+100% to -100%** and back.
segments.tr: Nhu cầu cấp nhà máy dao động từ **+100% đến -100%** và trở lại.

segments.src: Nobody behaved irrationally.
segments.tr: Không ai hành động không hợp lý.

segments.src: Every single person made a locally sensible decision with the information they had.
segments.tr: Mỗi một người đã đưa ra một quyết định có ý nghĩa cục bộ với thông tin mà họ có.

segments.src: That's the bullwhip.
segments.tr: Đó là roi queo.

segments.src: And it's why Walmart shares point-of-sale data directly with suppliers, why vendor-managed inventory exists, and why "everyday low pricing" is a supply chain strategy, not just a marketing slogan — it kills cause #3.
segments.tr: Và đó là lý do tại sao Walmart chia sẻ dữ liệu điểm bán hàng trực tiếp với các nhà cung cấp, tại sao quản lý hàng tồn kho của nhà cung cấp tồn tại, và tại sao "giá thấp hàng ngày" là một chiến lược chuỗi cung ứng, không chỉ là một slogan tiếp thị — nó loại bỏ nguyên nhân #3.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## Tóm Tắt 3 Dòng

segments.src: 1. A supply chain is a network of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and 3PLs moving three things: product downstream, money upstream, and information both ways.
segments.tr: 1. Chuỗi cung ứng là một mạng lưới gồm các nhà cung cấp, nhà sản xuất, nhà phân phối, nhà bán lẻ và 3PL chuyển ba thứ: sản phẩm xuôi dòng, tiền ngược dòng, và thông tin cả hai chiều.

segments.src: 2. The value chain is a different lens on the same steps — it asks where cost is incurred and where value is actually added.
segments.tr: 2. Chuỗi giá trị là một lăng kính khác trên cùng các bước — nó hỏi chi phí được phát sinh ở đâu và giá trị được thêm vào thực sự ở đâu.

segments.src: 3. The bullwhip effect is demand distortion amplifying upstream; its cure is better shared information, smaller/more frequent orders, stable pricing, and allocation rules that don't reward inflated orders.
segments.tr: 3. Hiệu ứng roi queo là sự biến dạng nhu cầu khuếch đại thượng nguồn; cách chữa trị là thông tin chia sẻ tốt hơn, các đơn hàng nhỏ hơn/thường xuyên hơn, giá cố định, và các quy tắc phân bổ không khen thưởng các đơn hàng phóng đại.

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kiểm Tra Tự Thân

segments.src: **1.** A company that sells components directly to a manufacturer is called a:
segments.tr: **1.** Một công ty bán các thành phần trực tiếp cho một nhà sản xuất được gọi là:

segments.src: - (A) Tier-2 supplier
segments.tr: - (A) Nhà cung cấp cấp 2

segments.src: - (B) Tier-1 supplier
segments.tr: - (B) Nhà cung cấp cấp 1

segments.src: - (C) 3PL
segments.tr: - (C) 3PL

segments.src: - (D) Distributor
segments.tr: - (D) Nhà phân phối

segments.src: **2.** O/X — The bullwhip effect happens because someone in the chain is behaving irrationally or incompetently.
segments.tr: **2.** Đúng/Sai — Hiệu ứng roi queo xảy ra vì ai đó trong chuỗi hành động không hợp lý hoặc không có năng lực.

segments.src: **3.** Which of the following would most likely *reduce* the bullwhip effect?
segments.tr: **3.** Cái nào sau đây sẽ *giảm* hiệu ứng roi queo?

segments.src: - (A) Running a deep 30%-off promotion every quarter
segments.tr: - (A) Chạy một chương trình khuyến mãi 30% sâu mỗi quý

segments.src: - (B) Switching from weekly orders to one large monthly truckload
segments.tr: - (B) Chuyển từ các đơn hàng hàng tuần sang một chuyến xe tải hàng tháng lớn

segments.src: - (C) Sharing real point-of-sale data with upstream suppliers
segments.tr: - (C) Chia sẻ dữ liệu điểm bán hàng thực với các nhà cung cấp thượng nguồn

segments.src: - (D) Allocating scarce supply in proportion to order size
segments.tr: - (D) Phân bổ nguồn cung thiếu hụt tương ứng với kích thước đơn hàng

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật Ngữ Hôm Nay

segments.src: - **Supply chain** — The network of organizations that moves a product from raw material to end customer.
segments.tr: - **Chuỗi cung ứng** — Mạng lưới các tổ chức chuyển một sản phẩm từ nguyên liệu thô đến khách hàng cuối cùng.

segments.src: - **Value chain** — A framework for analyzing where cost is added and where value is created across a firm's activities.
segments.tr: - **Chuỗi giá trị** — Một khung để phân tích chi phí được thêm vào ở đâu và giá trị được tạo ra ở đâu trên các hoạt động của công ty.

segments.src: - **Bullwhip effect** — The upstream amplification of demand variability caused by distorted information.
segments.tr: - **Hiệu ứng roi queo** — Sự khuếch đại thượng nguồn của biến động nhu cầu do thông tin biến dạng gây ra.

segments.src: - **Lead time** — The elapsed time between placing an order and receiving it; longer lead times force bigger buffers and worsen the bullwhip.
segments.tr: - **Thời gian giao hàng** — Thời gian trôi qua giữa việc đặt hàng và nhận nó; những thời gian giao hàng dài hơn buộc bộ đệm lớn hơn và làm trầm trọng hơn roi queo.

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics)** — An outside provider that handles transportation, warehousing, or fulfillment on a company's behalf.
segments.tr: - **3PL (logistics bên thứ ba)** — Một nhà cung cấp bên ngoài xử lý vận chuyển, lưu trữ, hoặc hoàn thành đơn hàng thay mặt công ty.

segments.src: *정답: 1) B — tier numbering counts hops away from the manufacturer, so the direct supplier is tier-1.
segments.tr: *Đáp án: 1) B — Đánh số cấp đếm các bước lên từ nhà sản xuất, vì vậy nhà cung cấp trực tiếp là cấp 1.

segments.src: 2) X — the whole point is that bullwhip emerges from locally rational decisions; each tier optimizes with only the information it can see.
segments.tr: 2) Sai — toàn bộ vấn đề là roi queo nổi lên từ các quyết định hợp lý cục bộ; mỗi cấp tối ưu hóa với chỉ thông tin mà nó có thể nhìn thấy.

segments.src: 3) C — shared POS data lets upstream partners forecast off real demand instead of off someone else's order.
segments.tr: 3) C — dữ liệu POS được chia sẻ cho phép các đối tác thượng nguồn dự báo dựa trên nhu cầu thực tế thay vì dựa trên đơn hàng của người khác.

segments.src: (A) is price fluctuation, (B) is order batching, and (D) is exactly the rationing rule that triggers shortage gaming — all three are classic bullwhip causes.*
segments.tr: (A) là biến động giá, (B) là đặt hàng theo lô, và (D) chính xác là quy tắc định tỷ lệ kích hoạt trò chơi thiếu hụt — cả ba đều là các nguyên nhân roi queo cổ điển.*
